decisions.reason: As a close-to-core finishing product with no negative market signal yet, it is still a low-cost option worth keeping while demand uncertainty resolves.

Because the UV spot varnishing system is more distant from the established portfolio and likely needs more commercial validation, its drop risk is higher, but the recent launch and lack of clear failure still favor keeping the option open.
This sheet preparation module builds directly on the firm's existing workflow-oriented offer, so it is cheap to carry strategically and sensible to retain.
The B2 multifinisher appears strategically important, was given prominent launch visibility, and fits the move toward automated integrated finishing, so management would likely continue backing it.
A hybrid saddle stitcher sits close to the firm's core booklet-making and binding business, making it a plausible portfolio extension that should be kept absent bad results.
The folding add-on already shows a named customer application and extends an existing system, which lowers uncertainty and makes withdrawal unlikely.
